initial_requirements: California Department of Transportation District 11 needs to replace the aging I-15 Reversible Lane Control System application. Traffic operators should be able to open and close reversible lanes for peak periods and special events, observe field-device and overall system status, issue control commands, configure operations, and generate reports. Authorized users and connected transportation systems should also receive relevant operational data through controlled local or remote access.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What are the top business objectives and success criteria for replacing the I-15 Reversible Lane Control System, especially in terms of operational improvements, safety, reliability, and support for peak-period or special-event lane management?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
The main business objective is to replace an aging system with something that operators can trust day to day, especially during the morning and evening reversals and during special events when traffic demand is higher than normal. We want faster, more consistent lane control decisions, better visibility into field-device and system status, and fewer manual workarounds when something goes wrong.
Success for us would mean the system improves safety by reducing the chance of incorrect lane states or delayed transitions, and it gives operators clear status and command feedback so they know the lanes are actually in the intended configuration. It also needs to be reliable enough that we can depend on it during peak periods and event traffic, with strong availability, straightforward recovery when devices fail, and enough operational reporting to show that lane changes are happening as planned.

slots.name: project_goals
slots.value: Replace the aging I-15 Reversible Lane Control System with a trusted, reliable system that supports day-to-day operations, morning and evening reversals, and special events; improve safety, reduce incorrect lane states and delayed transitions, increase visibility into field-device and system status, reduce manual workarounds, and provide operational reporting and clear command/status feedback.

slots.name: stakeholder_roles
slots.value: Traffic operators are the primary users; the system also serves authorized users and connected transportation systems that need operational data through controlled local or remote access.

slots.name: functional_needs
slots.value: Support opening and closing reversible lanes for peak periods and special events; observe field-device and overall system status; issue control commands; configure operations; generate reports; provide clear status and command feedback; and distribute relevant operational data to authorized users and connected transportation systems via controlled local or remote access.

slots.name: business_rules
slots.value: Lane control decisions must ensure the lanes are in the intended configuration, with operations supporting morning/evening reversals and special-event traffic management; lane changes should occur as planned and be reflected accurately in operator feedback and reports.

slots.name: data_entities
slots.value: Field-device status, overall system status, lane state/configuration, control commands, operational configuration settings, operational reports, and lane-change activity records.

slots.name: constraints
slots.value: Must support controlled local or remote access for authorized users and connected transportation systems; must be dependable during peak periods and special events; must provide strong availability and straightforward recovery when devices fail.

slots.name: quality_concerns
slots.value: High reliability, strong availability, safety, clear and timely operator feedback, consistency in lane control decisions, and straightforward recovery from device failures.

slots.name: boundary_conditions
slots.value: Special events, peak-period traffic, morning and evening reversals, and device failure conditions that require recovery and reduce manual workarounds.
